name: Shamir
overview: Shamir was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically descending from the family of Izhar, a branch of Kohath, who was a son of Levi. He is uniquely identified as the son of Micah and the grandson of Uzziel, situating him within the Levitical genealogies important for priestly and temple service roles. This lineage is noted in 1 Chronicles 24:24, linking him to the Levitical divisions.
namesAndTitles: The name Shamir means 'briers' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name without indication of divine origin. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:24 and does not carry a special title or additional meaning beyond its literal sense.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shamir as the son of Micah, who was the son of Uzziel, establishing a clear paternal lineage within the Levitical family of Izharites. No other family relationships are documented beyond this in the given references.
scriptureSignificance: Shamir's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, which were crucial for organizing the priestly duties and temple services in ancient Israel. As a descendant of Uzziel through Micah, Shamir represents one of the heads of the Levitical families assigned to specific priestly divisions. This organization was vital for the orderly worship of God, as outlined in 1 Chronicles 24:24.
